observation.visible_scene: A night seascape under an active aurora. A dark, flat horizon line with low clouds sits above a calm, near-black water surface that catches faint magenta reflections on the left. The sky is dominated by curtains of purple/magenta light interwoven with teal-green edges, brightest in a vertical column left of center and in a sweeping arc on the right.
visible_changes: The aurora curtains undergo slow, continuous morphing and rippling rather than discrete motion: the bright central magenta-teal column shifts slightly and changes its lean and fringe shape over the segment.
The right-side arc's lower green edge rises and the magenta above it spreads, so the arc appears to extend and deform upward across the frames.
The purple banding on the left and the teal glow along the lower aurora edges subtly intensify and reshape from frame 1 to frame 41.
The horizon line, cloud layer, and water surface remain essentially fixed in position, indicating the dominant motion is the aurora itself, not camera translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: The segment is a temporal crop; the onset and eventual dissipation of this auroral display are not shown.
Whether the slow drift is purely atmospheric motion or includes minor camera movement cannot be settled from the static horizon alone.
Conditions before t=0 and after t=3.2s in the longer source are unseen.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and magnitude of the aurora's drift (deformation vs. translation) is hard to pin down because the structures are diffuse.
Changes in the water's faint reflection may stem from aurora brightness variation or from small surface ripples; this is not distinguishable.
No editing seam is visible; all frames appear to belong to one continuous shot.
